clue.text: Sculptor trying Job's patience

indicators.note: something trying puts these letters under strain, so they are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: An artist whose slow work would test even the biblical Job's famous patience.
explanation.walkthrough: 'trying' rearranges JOBSPATIENCE, the possessive S included, into the sculptor's full name. Job is the long-suffering figure of the Old Testament.
explanation.definitionFit: Sir Jacob Epstein was an American-born British sculptor of the twentieth century, famous for bronzes and stone carvings.

clue.text: Luck of the draw for man on grass?

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second, so this says which comes first

parts.note: Jack is a stock man's name in crosswords
grass and pot are both slang for cannabis

explanation.surface: A lucky fellow lounging on the lawn wins big in a raffle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' places JACK above POT in the down light; the surface lets 'man on grass' read as someone on a lawn, not a man on drugs.
explanation.definitionFit: A jackpot is a big prize won by chance, so it is the reward luck of the draw can bring.

clue.text: Military expedition caused havoc with capture of Richard I

indicators.note: the rearranged letters capture, or hold inside them, the letter that follows
havoc throws the word caused into disorder, so its letters are rearranged
Richard I read as letter number one of Richard picks its initial

explanation.surface: King Richard I, the Lionheart, captured on campaign and causing chaos.
explanation.walkthrough: 'havoc' turns CAUSED into CUSADE; 'with capture of' takes in R, which 'Richard I' gives as the first letter of Richard. The surface fits, since Richard I went on a Crusade and was captured coming home.
explanation.definitionFit: A crusade was originally a military expedition by European Christians to the Holy Land.

clue.text: See one store in unfinished block

indicators.note: one piece is set inside the other
unfinished means the last letter of the word is left off

parts.note: a brick is a building block
I is the Roman numeral for one
a store is a shop

explanation.surface: Look: one shop has been built into a half-made block of buildings.
explanation.walkthrough: 'See' looks like a verb, but it is the noun: a bishop's diocese. 'unfinished' cuts BRICK to BRIC, and 'in' sets ISHOP inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A see is a bishop's area of authority, and a bishopric is the same diocese or office.

clue.text: Model problem

definitions.meaning: someone who poses for an artist or photographer is a model
a puzzling question or tricky problem is often called this

explanation.definitionFit: A poser is both one who poses, as a model does, and a baffling question that is hard to solve.

clue.text: Shaking the rump makes rabbit animated

indicators.note: shaking jiggles the letters of the following words about into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A cartoon bunny wiggles its bottom to come to life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shaking' rearranges THERUMP. The rabbit is the one in Disney's Bambi, famous for thumping its foot.
explanation.definitionFit: Thumper is the young rabbit in the Disney cartoon Bambi, so he is an animated rabbit by name.

clue.text: Ireland's first chief of police in Russia joins Pole from part of southern Europe

indicators.note: first takes only the opening letter of the word before it

parts.note: Lavrentiy Beria headed Stalin's secret police in the Soviet Union
N stands for the North Pole

explanation.surface: An Irish officer joins a Russian police chief and a Polish man in a European alliance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pole' looks like a nationality but is a magnetic pole, N. The answer is an adjective, as the definition is.
explanation.definitionFit: Iberian describes Spain and Portugal, on the Iberian Peninsula in Europe's south-west, so it means belonging to that part.

clue.text: Such robbery from handbags mars outing

indicators.note: an outing takes the letters of these words out and puts them back in another order

explanation.surface: A trip out is spoilt when bags are snatched.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outing' rearranges HANDBAGSMARS; the robbery is the kind where a window is broken and goods are grabbed.
explanation.definitionFit: A smash-and-grab is a theft by breaking a shop window and seizing goods, so it names this type of robbery.

clue.text: Dummies scoff at good times

parts.note: to scoff at is to mock
ups, as in ups and downs, are good times

explanation.surface: Fools jeer at others when things are going well.
explanation.definitionFit: Mock-ups are dummy models of something planned, made for display or testing.

clue.text: Contract bridge player's ploy

definitions.meaning: to contract is to shrink or press together
in the card game bridge, a tactic forcing opponents to discard winning cards

explanation.surface: The clue reads as the card game contract bridge and one player's tactic.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface runs 'Contract bridge' together as the name of the game; split it after 'Contract'.
explanation.definitionFit: To squeeze is to compress or contract, and in bridge a squeeze play forces damaging discards.

clue.text: Appliance for one who likes old farm vehicles?

parts.note: ex means former or old
a tractor is a farm vehicle; the plural is loose to fit the surface
a fan is an enthusiast

explanation.surface: A gadget for a collector of vintage farm machinery.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a phrase, the pieces describe someone who loves old tractors; the real answer is a kitchen or bathroom appliance.
explanation.definitionFit: An extractor fan is an electrical appliance that draws stale air or steam out of a room.

clue.text: Noodles one provided with game or cheese

parts.note: noodle is slang for a fool, as is sap
a means one
go is a Japanese board game

explanation.surface: A dish of noodles, offered with game or with cheese.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noodles' looks like pasta but means fools.
explanation.definitionFit: Sapsago is a hard green Swiss cheese flavoured with clover.

clue.text: Salesman is not to put on new coat

parts.note: a rep is a sales representative
ain't is colloquial for is not

explanation.surface: A salesman refuses to put on a new jacket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'coat' suggests clothing; it is a coat of paint.
explanation.definitionFit: To repaint is to give a surface a fresh coat of paint.

clue.text: "Craftiness that is ____ I rate as misrepresentation" (Shaw)

parts.note: craftiness, as in cunning, is art
i.e. stands for id est, that is

explanation.surface: A mock quotation from Shaw about craftiness and misrepresentation.
explanation.walkthrough: The blank's words build ART + IE; 'I rate as misrepresentation' gives the same letters again as an anagram. The Shaw is the bandleader Artie Shaw, not the playwright.
explanation.definitionFit: Artie Shaw was an American jazz clarinettist and big-band leader, so the first name completes this Shaw.

clue.text: Votes about further education? About Desperate Dan!

parts.note: re means about or concerning
re again means about

indicators.note: desperate signals that the name Dan is jumbled into another order

explanation.surface: Ballots on further education, and a comic-strip cowboy, Desperate Dan, in the middle of it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Desperate' rearranges DAN to NDA. Desperate Dan is a strongman in the British comic The Dandy.
explanation.definitionFit: Referenda are public votes on a single question, the plural of referendum.

clue.text: Nice cop, perhaps, impounding unknown substance derived from seaweed or fungus

indicators.note: to impound is to shut something in, so the first piece encloses the rest

parts.note: flic is French slang for a police officer, as in Nice in France
y is an unknown in algebra
agar is a jelly made from seaweed

explanation.surface: A friendly policeman seizes some suspicious seaweed or mushroom product.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nice' looks like kind but is the French city, pointing to French slang. 'impounding' puts YAGAR inside FLIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Fly agaric is a red and white spotted toadstool, a poisonous fungus.

clue.text: Opium-eater you would back to bear fruit

indicators.note: to bear is to carry, so the outer piece holds the other within it
back means the word for you would is turned around

parts.note: ye'd is an old contraction of you would
a quince is a hard pear-shaped fruit

explanation.surface: Someone is told to turn back and produce fruit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' reverses the archaic contraction to give DEY, and 'to bear' wraps it round the fruit. The surface's 'bear fruit' is an idiom, but here bear means carry.
explanation.definitionFit: Thomas De Quincey wrote Confessions of an English Opium-Eater, a nickname that stuck to him.

clue.text: Former question by university don agitated and upset graduate

indicators.note: agitated stirs the word don into a new order
upset in a down clue turns the word upward, so its letters run backwards

parts.note: an MA is a Master of Arts, a graduate

explanation.surface: An academic, questioned at his university, gets flustered and so does a graduate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'agitated' turns DON into OND; 'upset' turns MA into AM.
explanation.definitionFit: Quondam is a formal word for former or one-time, as in a quondam friend.

clue.text: Line marked on chart revealed his boat at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused, so these letters are muddled into a new order

explanation.surface: A man's boat, out on the ocean, shows up as a line on a sea chart.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' rearranges HISBOAT; 'revealed' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: An isobath is a line on a map or chart joining points of equal depth under water.

clue.text: Viz gives advice on how to use a trailer

definitions.meaning: viz is short for videlicet, meaning namely

definitions.text: advice on how to use a trailer
definitions.meaning: the instruction to pull it behind a car

explanation.surface: A satirical comic offers towing tips.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense reads the answer as two words, an instruction to haul the trailer behind a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: To wit and viz both mean namely, introducing an explanation or list.

clue.text: Transport Gibson in hamper

parts.note: a tram is a form of public transport
Mel Gibson is the Australian-American actor

explanation.surface: Mel Gibson is carried in a picnic basket.
explanation.walkthrough: 'hamper' looks like a basket; it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: To trammel is to hamper or restrict someone's freedom of action.

clue.text: Holiday money spent abroad is raised in Houston

parts.note: Whit, or Whitsun, is a British spring holiday

indicators.note: raised in a down clue lifts the word upward, so it reads backwards

parts.note: the yen is the currency of Japan

explanation.surface: Holiday cash spent overseas is raised in a Texas city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is raised' turns YEN to NEY. Houston is not the city but the singer.
explanation.definitionFit: Whitney Houston was the American pop and soul singer, so her first name goes with Houston.

clue.text: Unearth little jumper that's quite French

parts.note: roo is short for kangaroo, a jumping animal
tout is French for quite or entirely

explanation.surface: Dig up a small sweater that looks rather French.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jumper' suggests a British sweater, but it is a kangaroo.
explanation.definitionFit: To root out is to dig up or find and remove, which is to unearth.

clue.text: Try to get up about five to see telly

indicators.note: about means around, so the turned word goes round the letter
getting up in a down clue makes the word read upwards, so backwards

parts.note: to try is to test
V is the Roman numeral for five

explanation.surface: Struggling to rise at about five to watch the TV.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to get up' turns TEST to TSET, and 'about' puts V inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Telly is British slang for television, and a TV set is the receiver itself.

clue.text: Craftsman less inclined to work after midnight

indicators.note: after places the first piece before the second in the answer

parts.note: the middle letter of the word night
lazier means less inclined to work

explanation.surface: A worker is reluctant to carry on past midnight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'midnight' reads as the mid of night, its middle letter G.
explanation.definitionFit: A glazier is a craftsman who cuts and fits glass in windows.

clue.text: Villains crazy about article by Lawrence

indicators.note: about means around, so the first piece goes around the rest

parts.note: bats is slang for crazy
a is the indefinite article
D.H. Lawrence was the English novelist

explanation.surface: Wild critics rave over an essay by Lawrence.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' puts ADH inside BATS.
explanation.definitionFit: A bad hat is an old British expression for a rogue or villain.

clue.text: Italian city in a different country

parts.note: Roma is the Italian name of Rome

indicators.note: different means the letters of in a are made into a different order

explanation.surface: A city in Italy found in another nation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'different' turns IN A into NIA.
explanation.definitionFit: Romania is a country in south-eastern Europe.

clue.text: They claim pal is suffering with stress

indicators.note: suffering means these letters are in a bad way and fall into another order

explanation.surface: Some people insist their friend is going through a hard time.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is suffering' rearranges THEYCLAIMPAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Emphatically means forcefully, with stress or emphasis on what is said.
